фраза: You are working in a copy of a repository that holds the harness of an AI agent: the prompts and the code that run the agent on tasks.
README.md describes the layout; the harness is in src/.
This directory is everything there is to read: the agent's recorded runs are in logs/; the benchmark is not here.
The agent's failed runs were studied by a colleague; their observations are in the first message.
The runs are in logs/: trust your colleague initially; if you are confused, you may check the logs.
Your goal: change src/ so that the agent fails fewer tasks.
Each observation that points to a weakness of the harness is a candidate for a change.
An observation may also be inaccurate, or point to something the harness cannot change; what it says about src/ you can check by reading src/.
The same harness runs on every task the agent gets, so aim for changes that help on tasks in general.
A change may be to a prompt or to the code.
bash(command): a read-only shell in the working directory.
Programs: :, [, [[, awk, basename, break, cat, cd, column, comm, command, continue, cut, diff, dirname, echo, expr, false, find, grep, head, jq, ls, nl, od, pas
Pipes, ';', '&&', '||', $(...), for/while loops and if work.
Nothing can be written with it.
Output longer than 8000 characters is truncated, so read big files in parts (sed -n '40,90p' FILE, head, tail) and search with grep -n.
The shell is bash 3.2 with macOS/BSD utilities:
GNU-only options are missing (use grep -E, not grep -P; no find -printf).
python3 is available (standard library; no network, nothing can be written).

To write into an empty file or to create a new file in src/, give an empty old_string.

`src/` — the harness of the agent: the prompts and the code that run it on a task.
`hooks.py` — functions that `harness.py` calls;
`hook_types.py` — what each of them is given and may return.
`starting_prompt.md` is the system prompt.
`bridge.py` — connection to the benchmark.
`logs/` — runs of the harness in `src/` as it was at the start.
`run_N.jsonl` — one episode as a stream of events, one per line.
`bridge` — a call through the bridge (`start`;
`send`: a model reply handed to the task, `turn` — its number, `not_shown` — the task's messages the harness did not put into the conversation;
`end`: how the task ended the episode — `finished`, `step limit`, `error` with `detail`);
`prompt` — the system message built from `src/starting_prompt.md`;
`env` — a message of the task, as the model received it;
`harness` — other messages from the harness (`from`: its file in `src/`).
The `message` fields in order are the conversation as the model saw it.
`tests/rerun.py` — replays the runs recorded in `logs/` on the current `src/`.
The model's replies and the task's messages are taken from the log, so neither the model nor the benchmark is called.
As long as what the harness gives the model and the task is the same as in the log, the log still describes the run; at the first place where it differs, the re
`-` what the log has there, `+` what the harness does now.
From that point on the rest of the log no longer applies.
It also shows the hooks whose answer changed compared with `src/` as it was at the start (a copy of it is in `tests/orig_src/`).
`no changes` means that in those runs the current `src/` gives the model and the task exactly what the log has.
`python3 tests/rerun.py` prints one line per group of runs that behave the same way;
`python3 tests/rerun.py N` shows run N in detail, with the line of `logs/run_N.jsonl`.

`tests/runs.py` — reads the runs recorded in `logs/`.
`python3 tests/runs.py steps N` prints run N in short, one line per model call: its number, the log line, what the model sent → the first line of what came back
